We need propose retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <=9999. Need to output JSON route.

We need to find retrosynthetic steps using templates. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria to find disconnections. The target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's analyze structure: It's a sulfonamide linking a tolyl (p-tolyl) to a phenyl sulfonyl attached to a phenyl with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-para-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH (anilide). Actually the amide is attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So we have a secondary amide with an aniline substituent.

Potential retrosynthesis: disconnection at sulfonamide formation: combine p-tolyl amine (p-toluidine) with sulfonyl chloride derived from phenyl sulfonyl group attached to the rest of molecule (maybe 4-(E)-...?). Another disconnection: amide formation between aniline and acrylic acid derivative (trans- cinnamoyl). So we could have two steps: first form amide, then sulfonamide.

Step 1: Amide formation: React aniline (c3ccccc3N) with (E)-4-(4-(p-tolyl)sulfonyl)phenylacrylic acid? Actually the acid part includes the phenyl-sulfonyl phenyl group attached to the double bond. So we need a carboxylic acid: (E)-4-(4-(p-tolyl)sulfonyl)phenylacrylic acid (i.e., 4-(p-tolylsulfonyl) cinnamic acid). Then amide coupling with aniline gives the target.

Step 2: Sulfonyl chloride formation: from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to phenyl ring (the phenyl bearing the double bond). So we need to attach sulfonyl group onto that phenyl. Could start from 4-bromophenylacrylic acid, then sulfonylate with p-tolylsulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonylation of aromatic amine: we need sulfonyl chloride reacting with amine (p-toluidine). So we could have p-toluidine + 4-(phenyl) sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to phenyl ring (the phenyl that is attached to the double bond). The sulfonyl group is S(=O)2 attached to that phenyl and to the p-tolyl amine. So the sulfonyl chloride would be 4-(E)-cinnamoyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is derived from the phenyl-sulfonyl part: 4-(E)-cinnamoyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (i.e., 4-(E)-cinnamoyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). Then reacting with p-toluidine gives sulfonamide.

Thus route: Step A: sulfonyl chloride synthesis from 4-bromobenzene? Could be via chlorosulfonation of 4-(E)-cinnamoyl phenyl? Might be complex.

Alternative: Use two steps: first form sulfonamide between p-toluidine and 4-(E)-cinnamoyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial?). Maybe that sulfonyl chloride is not commercially available.

We need leaves commercially available chemicals. Could we use commercially available sulfonyl chloride: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) is common, but our sulfonyl group is attached to phenyl, not to tolyl. Actually TsCl is p-tolyl-SO2Cl. If we react TsCl with aniline (p-aminophenyl) we get p-tolyl-sulfonamide attached to aniline. But our target has p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl that also bears the cinnamoyl amide. So we could start from p-toluenesulfonyl chloride reacting with 4-aminophenyl (para-aminophenyl) that is further functionalized with the cinnamoyl amide. So we could first form amide on 4-aminophenyl (aniline) with cinnamic acid derivative, then sulfonylate the resulting aniline? But sulfonylation of aniline after amide may be hindered.

Better: first sulfonylate p-toluidine with 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Not.

Maybe we can use three steps: 1) Form amide between aniline and trans-cinnamic acid (commercial). That gives trans-cinnamoylaniline (C6H5-CH=CH-CO-NH-C6H5). Then 2) Sulfonylate the aniline nitrogen (now part of amide) is not nucleophilic. So not.

Alternative: Use sulfonyl chloride derived from p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (TsCl) reacting with 4-aminophenyl that already has the cinnamoyl amide attached via its amine? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (aniline). So the aniline nitrogen is part of amide, not free. The sulfonamide nitrogen is the p-toluidine nitrogen. So we need p-toluidine (p-CH3C6H4NH2) reacting with sulfonyl chloride derived from phenyl that has the cinnamoyl amide attached at para position. So we need 4-(E)-cinnamoyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (4-(E)-cinnamoyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). Is that commercially available? Possibly not.

Maybe we can reverse: Use sulfonyl chloride TsCl (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) reacting with aniline that is substituted with the cinnamoyl amide at para position. That would give p-tolyl-sulfonamide attached to phenyl bearing the amide. So we need 4-(E)-cinnamoyl aniline (para-aminocinnamamide). That is aniline with amide at para? Actually we need aniline where the para position has the cinnamoyl amide attached via carbonyl to the aniline? Wait the target: phenyl ring attached to sulfonyl group, and also attached to the trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH. The amide is attached to the phenyl via the carbonyl carbon attached to the phenyl (i.e., phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH). So the phenyl bearing the sulfonyl group also bears the trans-CH=CH-CO-... at para position? Actually SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to S(=O)(=O) to p-tolyl. So the phenyl (c2ccc...cc2) is attached to sulfonyl group at one position (maybe para) and the cinnamoyl amide at another position (para relative?). The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 indicates the substituent is at position 1 of phenyl (attached to sulfonyl) and the side chain at position 4 (para). So we need a phenyl with both sulfonyl chloride and a para substituent that is the cinnamoyl amide.

Thus we could start from 4-bromo-phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Not.

Maybe we can use a Suzuki coupling to install the side chain after sulfonamide formation. For simplicity, we can propose a 3-step route: 1) Start from p-toluidine (commercial) and p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) to make p-tolyl-sulfonamide (p-tolylSO2NH-p-tolyl). Not correct.

Given time, maybe we can propose a plausible route using commercially available building blocks: p-toluidine, 4-bromobenzaldehyde, cinnamic acid, etc. Use Suzuki coupling to attach phenyl.

But we need to output JSON with template IDs. We need to retrieve templates. Let's search for amide formation template.
